bull_bear.body:
- Established manufacturing footprint across three sites (Umred, Dahej and the upcoming Butibori facility) spanning CNG, industrial, medical and high-pressure cylinders
- Diversified product portfolio across CNG, industrial gases, medical gases and emerging clean-energy applications, which management cites as supporting sustainable expansion
- Established customer relationships, cited by management alongside manufacturing capability as the basis for capitalising on CGD and CNG demand
- Early move into Type-IV composite cylinder technology, positioning the Company for hydrogen mobility and next-generation high-pressure storage
- Part of the Confidence group, being a subsidiary of Confidence Petroleum India Limited, which holds 61.87% of the equity share capital
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Enterprise risk oversight depends on a Board-level Risk Management Committee rather than a dedicated Chief Risk Officer — This bundle shows the RMC formulating and monitoring the risk management policy and supporting the Board on Enterprise Risk Management, with the appointment, removal and remuneration of a Chief Risk Officer only 'if any' subject to RMC review — so there is no disclosed standing CRO. The policy is reviewed at least once in two years, a relatively infrequent cadence for a company facing fast-moving alternative-fuel technology shifts.
- Financial, operational and sectoral risk exposure identified under the risk management framework — The RMC's mandate expressly requires a framework for identification of internal and external risks specifically faced by the listed entity, in particular financial, operational and sectoral risks, indicating management treats these as the principal categories of exposure.
- Sustainability / ESG-related risk — Named explicitly in the RMC's terms of reference as a risk category the risk-identification framework must cover, alongside financial, operational and sectoral risks.
- Information and cyber security risk — Named explicitly in the RMC's terms of reference as a risk category the risk-identification framework must cover, and mitigation measures including systems and processes for internal control of identified risks must be specified.
- Key-person and promoter-family concentration in executive management — The Board committees disclosed here show Mr. Nitin Khara as the sole Executive Director member of both the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and the Risk Management Committee, so executive representation on risk and investor oversight rests with one promoter-family executive.
- Governance committee concentration — the same two independent directors chair and staff the key oversight committees — Mr. Vaibhav Dedhia chairs both the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and the Risk Management Committee, with Mr. Sumant Sutaria and Mrs. Mansi Deogirkar the only other independent members disclosed, leaving limited independent bench depth for oversight.
- Investor-grievance handling exposure — The Company received 4 complaints during the financial year, all resolved with none pending as at 31 March 2026; the SRC's remit covers share transfer/transmission, non-receipt of annual reports and declared dividends, and oversight of the Registrar and Transfer Agent's performance.
- CSR is voluntary rather than statutory, so community/social spend is not underpinned by a Section 135 obligation — Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 is stated as not yet applicable to the Company; a CSR Committee has been constituted proactively, meaning social-licence activity depends on discretionary commitment rather than a statutory floor.

business.body: CFEL, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacturing of CNG cylinders, industrial gas cylinders, medical gas cylinders, high-pressure cylinders and cascades catering to diverse industrial and energy sectors. Manufacturing is carried out through Confidence Enterprises Private Limited (wholly owned, Umred, Maharashtra), Sarju Impex Limited (Dahej, Gujarat) and Silversky Exim Private Limited, which is establishing a Type-IV high-pressure composite cylinder facility at Butibori, Nagpur. The Company is itself a subsidiary of Confidence Petroleum India Limited and its equity shares are listed on BSE Limited.

outlook.body:
- Develop the Type-4 High-Pressure Composite Cylinder Project at Butibori, Nagpur through a subsidiary, positioning the Company in next-generation cylinder technology for CNG mobility and hydrogen transportation
- Strengthen the sourcing and supply network for CNG cylinders and high-pressure gas containment solutions to ensure uninterrupted product availability
- Enhance operational efficiency and expand customer relationships across CNG, industrial gases, medical gases and emerging clean-energy applications
- Invest in advanced technologies, process improvements and capacity enhancement initiatives to meet evolving customer requirements and global quality standards
- Build a future-ready organisation capable of serving both domestic and international markets
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's principal expansion is the Type-IV high-pressure composite cylinder manufacturing facility being established at Butibori, Nagpur through its subsidiary Silversky Exim Private Limited, described by the Chairman as having made continued progress during FY 2025-26. Management calls it a significant strategic milestone, expected on commissioning to strengthen the product portfolio and allow CFEL to serve hydrogen mobility, high-pressure gas storage and next-generation clean-energy applications; no commissioning date, capex quantum or capacity figure is stated in this bundle. Existing manufacturing is carried out at Umred, Maharashtra (through wholly owned subsidiary Confidence Enterprises Private Limited) and at Dahej, Gujarat (through subsidiary Sarju Impex Limited). The Chairman also states the Company continues to invest in advanced technologies, process improvements and capacity enhancement initiatives, and that it strengthened its sourcing and supply network for CNG cylinders and high-pressure gas containment solutions during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's transition toward cleaner energy is driving robust growth in demand for advanced gas storage and transportation solutions
- Government emphasis on expanding natural gas infrastructure, promoting cleaner fuels and increasing the share of natural gas in the country's energy mix is creating opportunities across the energy value chain
- Global energy landscape increasingly embracing clean fuels and green hydrogen, making Type-4 composite cylinders suitable for CNG mobility and hydrogen transportation

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Confidence Futuristic Energetech Limited manufactures CNG, industrial, medical and other high-pressure gas cylinders and cascades through its subsidiaries, reporting consolidated revenue of approximately ₹158 Crores in FY 2025-26.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: CFEL, through its subsidiaries, is engaged in the manufacturing of CNG cylinders, industrial gas cylinders, medical gas cylinders, high-pressure cylinders and cascades catering to diverse industrial and energy sectors. Manufacturing is carried out through Confidence Enterprises Private Limited (wholly owned, Umred, Maharashtra), Sarju Impex Limited (Dahej, Gujarat) and Silversky Exim Private Limited, which is establishing a Type-IV high-pressure composite cylinder facility at Butibori, Nagpur. The Company is itself a subsidiary of Confidence Petroleum India Limited and its equity shares are listed on BSE Limited.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **High-pressure gas containment:** CNG cylinders, Industrial gas cylinders, Medical gas cylinders, High-pressure cylinders, Cascades
- **Composite cylinders (under development):** Type-IV high-pressure composite cylinders

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- CNG mobility and city gas distribution (CGD) network
- Industrial gases for steel, engineering, automotive, chemicals, petrochemicals, fabrication and manufacturing
- Healthcare / medical oxygen
- Emerging hydrogen storage and clean-energy applications
- India (domestic); Company states an objective of serving both domestic and international markets

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's transition toward cleaner energy is driving robust growth in demand for advanced gas storage and transportation solutions
- Government emphasis on expanding natural gas infrastructure, promoting cleaner fuels and increasing the share of natural gas in the country's energy mix is creating opportunities across the energy value chain
- Global energy landscape increasingly embracing clean fuels and green hydrogen, making Type-4 composite cylinders suitable for CNG mobility and hydrogen transportation

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Develop the Type-4 High-Pressure Composite Cylinder Project at Butibori, Nagpur through a subsidiary, positioning the Company in next-generation cylinder technology for CNG mobility and hydrogen transportation
- Strengthen the sourcing and supply network for CNG cylinders and high-pressure gas containment solutions to ensure uninterrupted product availability
- Enhance operational efficiency and expand customer relationships across CNG, industrial gases, medical gases and emerging clean-energy applications
- Invest in advanced technologies, process improvements and capacity enhancement initiatives to meet evolving customer requirements and global quality standards
- Build a future-ready organisation capable of serving both domestic and international markets

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's principal expansion is the Type-IV high-pressure composite cylinder manufacturing facility being established at Butibori, Nagpur through its subsidiary Silversky Exim Private Limited, described by the Chairman as having made continued progress during FY 2025-26. Management calls it a significant strategic milestone, expected on commissioning to strengthen the product portfolio and allow CFEL to serve hydrogen mobility, high-pressure gas storage and next-generation clean-energy applications; no commissioning date, capex quantum or capacity figure is stated in this bundle. Existing manufacturing is carried out at Umred, Maharashtra (through wholly owned subsidiary Confidence Enterprises Private Limited) and at Dahej, Gujarat (through subsidiary Sarju Impex Limited). The Chairman also states the Company continues to invest in advanced technologies, process improvements and capacity enhancement initiatives, and that it strengthened its sourcing and supply network for CNG cylinders and high-pressure gas containment solutions during the year.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established manufacturing footprint across three sites (Umred, Dahej and the upcoming Butibori facility) spanning CNG, industrial, medical and high-pressure cylinders
- Diversified product portfolio across CNG, industrial gases, medical gases and emerging clean-energy applications, which management cites as supporting sustainable expansion
- Established customer relationships, cited by management alongside manufacturing capability as the basis for capitalising on CGD and CNG demand
- Early move into Type-IV composite cylinder technology, positioning the Company for hydrogen mobility and next-generation high-pressure storage
- Part of the Confidence group, being a subsidiary of Confidence Petroleum India Limited, which holds 61.87% of the equity share capital

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Enterprise risk oversight depends on a Board-level Risk Management Committee rather than a dedicated Chief Risk Officer — This bundle shows the RMC formulating and monitoring the risk management policy and supporting the Board on Enterprise Risk Management, with the appointment, removal and remuneration of a Chief Risk Officer only 'if any' subject to RMC review — so there is no disclosed standing CRO. The policy is reviewed at least once in two years, a relatively infrequent cadence for a company facing fast-moving alternative-fuel technology shifts.
- Financial, operational and sectoral risk exposure identified under the risk management framework — The RMC's mandate expressly requires a framework for identification of internal and external risks specifically faced by the listed entity, in particular financial, operational and sectoral risks, indicating management treats these as the principal categories of exposure.
- Sustainability / ESG-related risk — Named explicitly in the RMC's terms of reference as a risk category the risk-identification framework must cover, alongside financial, operational and sectoral risks.
- Information and cyber security risk — Named explicitly in the RMC's terms of reference as a risk category the risk-identification framework must cover, and mitigation measures including systems and processes for internal control of identified risks must be specified.
- Key-person and promoter-family concentration in executive management — The Board committees disclosed here show Mr. Nitin Khara as the sole Executive Director member of both the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and the Risk Management Committee, so executive representation on risk and investor oversight rests with one promoter-family executive.
- Governance committee concentration — the same two independent directors chair and staff the key oversight committees — Mr. Vaibhav Dedhia chairs both the Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and the Risk Management Committee, with Mr. Sumant Sutaria and Mrs. Mansi Deogirkar the only other independent members disclosed, leaving limited independent bench depth for oversight.
- Investor-grievance handling exposure — The Company received 4 complaints during the financial year, all resolved with none pending as at 31 March 2026; the SRC's remit covers share transfer/transmission, non-receipt of annual reports and declared dividends, and oversight of the Registrar and Transfer Agent's performance.
- CSR is voluntary rather than statutory, so community/social spend is not underpinned by a Section 135 obligation — Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 is stated as not yet applicable to the Company; a CSR Committee has been constituted proactively, meaning social-licence activity depends on discretionary commitment rather than a statutory floor.
